title: Couche-Tard sees finish line for $8.6-billion takeover of Polish retailer Zabka Group
html:
Zabka's store in Warsaw. Couche-Tard announced the Zabka takeover, its biggest to date, in late July.Kacper Pempel/Reuters

Canadian retail giant Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. ATD-T, owner of the Circle K chain, is wrapping up its US$8.6-billion takeover of Polish retailer Zabka Group SA as investor attention now shifts to its next possible acquisition deal.

Couche-Tard won’t raise its current offer price for Zabka Group and it won’t extend the acceptance period for investors to tender their shares past Dec. 2, the company said in its earnings release late Tuesday. That suggests Couche-Tard believes it’s on track to win full ownership of Zabka, Bank of Montreal analyst Tamy Chen said in a research note.

The tender offer “continues with strong momentum, and the offer is now unconditional following all regulatory approvals,” Couche-Tard Chief Executive Alex Miller said in a statement.

The company had already cemented lock up agreements with key investors giving it control of 57 per cent of Zabka’s stock. It then offered 32 Polish zloty (about US$7.86 a share at current exchange rates) to investors holding the rest of the equity. It wasn’t immediately clear what percentage of additional shares it has won.

Laval, Que.-based Couche-Tard announced the Zabka takeover, its biggest to date, in late July. The deal widens the retail giant’s position in Europe against global rival 7-Eleven, bringing into the fold a dominant, technology-powered retailer that could transform the way Circle K operates in other countries.

With the Zabka purchase nearly complete, market attention will now turn to Couche-Tard’s next takeover opportunities. One name that has come back into the conversation is a familiar one: EG Group’s Cumberland Farms Ltd.

Four years ago, the Canadian company swapped proposals with Cumberland’s owners but the talks didn’t yield a deal, in part over disagreement over price. More recently, when Couche-Tard ended its year-long pursuit of Seven & i Holdings Co. in the summer of 2025, analysts identified Cumberland again as an acquisition opportunity.

Cumberland Farms’ owners were laying the groundwork for an initial public offering in New York as soon as this fall but the IPO has been delayed until next near amid takeover interest from infrastructure investment firm Stonepeak Partners LLP and other buyers, the Financial Times reported last month. Couche-Tard is believed to be among those exploring a purchase but the company has not commented on its intentions.

Billionaire brothers Mohsin and Zuber Issa co-founded EG Group in 2001 and later sold half the company to British buyout firm TDR Capital. The retailer launched with a single gas station in the Manchester area and quickly ballooned out across Europe in a buying binge facilitated by low-interest rates.

More recently, the retailer rebranded the bulk of its operations as Cumberland Farms, relocated its headquarters from the U.K. to Charlotte, N.C., and sold off hundreds of convenience stores across Italy, France, and Australia as part of a wider corporate reorganization effort to reduce debt.

TDR Capital and the Issa brothers are still focused on pursuing the IPO, the Financial Times reported. Still, selling the entire company would remove the uncertainty of an IPO at a time the market for new listings has become increasingly challenging.

Cumberland Farms holds a top-five market share in both Europe and the U.S., with about 3,200 sites in all as of March this year, according to a company filing to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. In Europe, it is concentrated in Germany and the Benelux countries.

Couche-Tard on Tuesday reported adjusted net earnings per share of US$0.84 for its latest quarter, an 8 per cent increase over the same period last year, as it generated higher profit margins on fuel and kept a check on selling, general and administrative expenses. The result beat the average analyst estimate of US$0.80.

Net earnings on a non-adjusted basis came in at US$691-million or US$0.75 per diluted share. Revenue, including store merchandise and fuel, rose to US$22.5-billion for the three-month period from US$17.9-billion in the same quarter last year.
summary: Investor attention now turns to next deal opportunity
